meridian_skill.description: Compile daily briefing with meeting context, active deals, and citation tracking
meridian_skill.name: briefing

outline.text: For each meeting on the calendar

sections.heading: Contract
lines: Meeting participants are resolved against the brain; gaps are explicitly flagged
Active deals and action items include deadlines and recency context
The briefing is read-only: no brain pages are created or modified unless the user explicitly requests it
Stale alerts surface pages relevant to today's context, not just all stale pages

sections.heading: Contract — steps
lines: Every fact in the briefing includes an inline `[Source: slug, updated DATE]` citation

sections.heading: Phases
lines: **Recent changes.** Pages updated in the last 24 hours:
What changed and why (read timeline entries from gbrain)
Updated in last 7 days
Have high activity (many recent timeline entries)
**Stale alerts.** From gbrain health check:
Pages flagged as stale that are relevant to today's meetings

sections.heading: Phases — steps 2
lines: use judgment to follow the Phases — steps 2 guidance:
**Pending consolidation footer** — when `pending_consolidation_count > 0`,
note `N facts await dream-cycle consolidation` so the operator can decide
whether to run `gbrain dream` before reading further

sections.heading: Phases — steps 3
lines: For each meeting on the calendar:

sections.heading: Phases — steps 4
lines: List deal pages in gbrain filtered to active status:
Deadlines approaching in the next 7 days

sections.heading: Phases — steps 6
lines: List person pages in gbrain sorted by recency:

sections.heading: GBrain-Native Context Loading
lines: Before generating any briefing, load context from gbrain systematically

sections.heading: Before a meeting
lines: For every attendee on the calendar invite:
`gbrain search "<attendee name>"` -- find their brain page
`gbrain get <slug>` -- load compiled truth, recent timeline, relationship context
If no page exists, note the gap ("No brain page for Sarah Chen -- consider enrichment")

sections.heading: Before an email reply — steps
lines: `gbrain search "<sender name>"` -- load sender context

sections.heading: Before an email reply — steps 2
lines: use judgment to follow the Before an email reply — steps 2 guidance:
Read their compiled truth to understand who they are, what they care about, and
your relationship history. This turns a cold reply into an informed one

sections.heading: Daily briefing queries — steps
lines: `gbrain query "active deals status"` -- deal pipeline snapshot
`gbrain query "meetings this week"` -- recent meeting pages with insights
`gbrain query "pending commitments follow-ups"` -- open threads and action items
`gbrain search --type person --sort updated --limit 10` -- people in play

sections.heading: Output Format
lines: codeblock:plain:

sections.heading: Back-Linking During Briefing — steps
lines: If the briefing creates or updates any brain pages (e.g., new meeting prep
pages, updated entity pages), the back-linking iron law applies: every entity
mentioned must have a back-link from their page. See `skills/_brain-filing-rules.md`

sections.heading: Citation in Briefings
lines: "Jane is CTO of Acme [Source: people/jane-doe, updated 2026-04-01]"

sections.heading: Citation in Briefings — steps
lines: When presenting facts from brain pages, include inline citations:

sections.heading: Citation in Briefings — steps 2
lines: use judgment to follow the Citation in Briefings — steps 2 guidance:
This lets the user trace any claim back to the brain page and assess freshness

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns
lines: **Stale context presented as current.** If a page hasn't been updated in 30+ days, flag the staleness explicitly rather than presenting it as fresh
**Modifying brain pages unprompted.** The briefing is read-only by default. Do not create or update pages unless the user explicitly requests it

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns — steps
lines: Never generate a briefing from memory alone; always query gbrain for current data
Uncited facts. Every claim must include `[Source: slug, updated DATE]`. A fact without a citation is unverifiable

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns — steps 2
lines: When a meeting participant has no brain page, say so. Silence about gaps hides ignorance

sections.heading: Tools Used
lines: Search gbrain by name (query)
Read a page from gbrain (get_page)
List pages in gbrain by type (list_pages)
Check gbrain health (get_health)
View timeline entries in gbrain (get_timeline)
